excerpt: Our current understanding suggests at least two general sources of catastrophic risk from increasingly powerful AI models.
paraphrase: Anthropic identifies at least two general sources of catastrophic risk from increasingly powerful models.

excerpt: For our initial commitments, we design our evaluations and safety measures with these risks in mind:
paraphrase: Initial commitments' evaluations and safety measures are designed around these two risk sources.

context_stem: Our current understanding suggests at least two general sources of catastrophic risk:
excerpt: Misuse: AI systems are dual-use technologies, and so as they become more powerful, there is an increasing risk that they will be used to intentionally cause large-scale harm, for example by helping individuals create CBRN3 or cyber threats.
paraphrase: Misuse risk arises because dual-use AI systems could increasingly help people cause large-scale harm, such as CBRN or cyber threats.

context_stem: Our current understanding suggests at least two general sources of catastrophic risk:
excerpt: Autonomy and replication: As AI systems continue to scale, they may become capable of increased autonomy that enables them to proliferate and, due to imperfections in current methods for steering such systems, potentially behave in ways contrary to the intent of their designers or users.
paraphrase: Autonomy and replication risk arises as scaling AI systems may enable increased autonomy and proliferation, with potential to act against designer or user intent due to imperfect steering methods.

excerpt: Such systems could become a source of catastrophic risk even if no one deliberately intends to misuse them.
paraphrase: Autonomy-related risk could produce catastrophe even absent any deliberate misuse.

excerpt: We are likely to revise and refine these ideas as our understanding of AI systems develops.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to revise these risk categorizations as understanding improves.

excerpt: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements, which are visualized below and expanded on in the rest of this document.
paraphrase: The initial commitments consist of several elements, visualized and explained further in the document.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements:
excerpt: ASL-2: The security and safety measures we commit to take with current state-of-the-art models, many of which we have previously committed to.
paraphrase: ASL-2 comprises security and safety measures for current state-of-the-art models, several of which were previously committed to.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements:
excerpt: ASL-3: A set of dangerous capabilities we think could arise in near-future models, along with the Containment Measures we commit to implement before training such a model, and the Deployment Measures we commit to take before deploying it.
paraphrase: ASL-3 defines dangerous capabilities anticipated in near-future models plus the containment measures required before training and deployment measures required before deploying such models.

excerpt: CBRN refers to the chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear domains. We use it mostly to refer to threats in those domains.
paraphrase: The footnote defines CBRN as chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear domains.

excerpt: We acknowledge that some of these domains will become more or less relevant for evaluation over time.
paraphrase: The footnote notes that CBRN domain relevance for evaluation may shift over time.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements:
excerpt: ASL-4 iterative commitment: We commit to define ASL-4 evaluations before we first train ASL-3 models (i.e. before continuing training beyond when ASL-3 evaluations are triggered).
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to defining ASL-4 evaluations before beginning training of ASL-3 models.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements: ASL-4 iterative commitment
excerpt: Similarly, we commit to define ASL-5 evaluations before training ASL-4 models, and so forth.
paraphrase: Anthropic will similarly define ASL-5 evaluations before training ASL-4 models, continuing this pattern.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements:
excerpt: Evaluation protocol: A protocol for when and how to evaluate models for dangerous capabilities, ensuring we detect warning signs before models require higher ASL safety measures.
paraphrase: An evaluation protocol specifies when and how to test models for dangerous capabilities to catch warning signs early.

context_stem: Our initial responsible scaling commitments consist of the following elements: Evaluation protocol
excerpt: We commit to pause training before a model's capability level outstrips the Containment Measures we have implemented.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to pausing training before a model's capability exceeds implemented containment measures.
